Is the definition of watermarking changing?

Watermarking used to mean an image embedded in the paper itself - like a leaf, or name, or portrait - that could only be viewed holographically from a certain angle. In a watermarked document, every page contains the same watermark to ensure that the entire document is authentic.

Yes. Watermarks used to be rendered visible by wetting a page, hence the name; an artifact produced in the paper manufacturing process. The term seems to have evolved.
